blocks.title: Choke
blocks.text: A choke is a coil of thick copper wire wound closely with a large number of turns over a laminated soft-iron core.

A choke is often modelled as a series RL circuit: a very small resistance R in series with an inductor of large inductive reactance XL = 2 pi f L (Fig 17.7 e, a photograph). Its inductance is very high because of the high permeability of the iron core. As its resistance is negligible, its power factor (cos theta) is almost zero and the phase difference between current and voltage is nearly 90 degrees, so practically no power is dissipated as heat.

items: A choke blocks high-frequency AC while allowing DC and low-frequency AC to pass; it filters high-frequency noise out of electronic circuits, giving a cleaner DC output.
Chokes are essential in switch-mode power supplies, helping to regulate voltage and filter switching noise.
They stop unwanted radio-frequency signals leaking out of circuits, protecting sensitive components.
In fluorescent lights a choke produces the high transient voltage needed to start the discharge through the gas in the tube.
Chokes limit the rate of change of current, preventing damage to insulation from sudden surges.

blocks.alt: A graph of reactance against frequency. A straight purple line from the origin rising steadily is XL = 2 pi f L, which blocks high frequencies. A teal curve that is very high at low frequency and falls towards the axis is XC = 1/(2 pi f C), which blocks low frequencies and DC. A note says that for DC (f = 0) XL = 0 and XC is infinite.
blocks.caption: Inductive and capacitive reactance against frequency (original graph).
blocks.long_description: An inductor and a capacitor behave in opposite ways: the inductor lets DC through and opposes fast changes, while the capacitor blocks DC and lets fast changes through.

blocks.title: Do you know?
blocks.text: Why do a capacitor and an inductor behave differently for AC and DC? For a DC supply f = 0, so XL = 2 pi f L = 0 and the inductor acts as a conductor, while XC = 1/(2 pi f C) = 1/0, which is infinite: the capacitor blocks DC but allows AC to pass.
